value.title: [Epic] I0 P0: Safe Ground: What Must Hold Before Anything Is Rewritten

data.name: stakeholder_overview
data.value:
A new session today is born in two steps an agent performs by following prose, then a third step that writes over whatever it finds. The agent is asked to pass a repository name by hand. That derivation has bound the wrong repository in production, and the write has destroyed a run that was still in the folder, handing back the identifier of the work it just erased.

This change has the server take the working directory, derive the repository from git at that checkout, create the session on a durable folder, and refuse any write that would replace a session already there. Landing 1 is the server half: derivation, occupancy refusal, and the tests that pin both. The bound repository is the checkout under work.

data.name: problem_statement
data.value:
A new session is born in two agent-executed derivation steps, then a third step that writes session.json over whatever the destination folder already holds. The agent is asked to pass owner/repo by hand; that derivation has bound the wrong repository in production — a name taken from a pull-request link, an empty directory where source was expected, a session discarded at 81,762 tokens. The write has destroyed a live run on resume: measured on a real work package, a cursor and one completed activity before the second dispatch, empty cursor and none after, five history events reduced to two, the same identifier throughout.

System: start_session and dispatch_child in registerResourceTools persist through writeSessionFile in the session store. Omit planning_folder and the session is born under os.tmpdir(); the first dispatch_child then calls ensurePlanningFolder and writeSessionFile, whose contract replaces whatever the folder holds. Both the first run and a resume put a child in slot zero and derive the same identifier. GitNexus rates writeSessionFile CRITICAL (six direct callers, nine processes, four modules). This work package is Landing 1 of three: server derivation and occupancy on main; corpus rewrite on workflows; deletion of transient create.

Impact: Severity critical (issue labels: bug, tech-debt, priority: highest). Scope: every fresh start_session that derives repo from prose, and every resume that re-promotes onto a dated slug already holding a session. Business impact: lost runs that look healthy; wrong-repo binds that proceed as if the checkout were present.

Success criteria: Landing 1 acceptance in the specification — working_directory derivation, durable create, occupancy refuse with files untouched, writeSessionFile contract unchanged, ten tests against the real store. Criteria that belong to Landings 2 and 3 are out of this run.

Constraints: do not change writeSessionFile's contract; add createSessionFile. Occupancy-refuse, not reattach. Bound repository is the checkout under work, not the host unless that is the checkout. Open-decision shape for derivation disagreements. Landing 1 only (no corpus rewrite, no transient-folder deletion).

Root cause: repository identity is a caller-supplied argument rather than a server-side read of git at the checkout; persist is unconditional, so a second create onto a derived slug replaces the first run and returns its identifier. All six problem-definition boxes are filled from the specification, change brief, and impact analysis.

data.name: classification_rationale
data.value:
Type is specific-cause-known: production is failing today (wrong-repo binds; resume wipe with measured loss of cursor, completed activities, and history), and both cooperating causes are identified — agent-derived repo, and unconditional writeSessionFile on promote and derived-slug create. This is fix-or-restore work, not an inventive improvement of a working path.

Complexity is complex: several viable approaches were weighed (reattach vs occupancy-refuse; occupancy on writeSessionFile vs a createSessionFile wrapper; host bind vs checkout bind), the trade-offs are reliability-versus-ceremony, and GitNexus rates writeSessionFile CRITICAL (6 direct callers, 9 processes, 4 modules). registerResourceTools, the call site Landing 1 must edit, is also CRITICAL (33 upstream symbols). The specification already chooses the cuts; remaining work is implementation of a known design, which is why a later path selection of skip-optional would diverge from this complexity rather than contradict the type.

data.name: stakeholder_overview
data.value:
This landing has the server take the working directory of the checkout under work, read that checkout's git origin as the bound repository, and create the session on a durable planning folder. If that folder already holds a session, the call names the folder and the existing identifier and leaves the files untouched. The persist function that writes every session stays as it is; occupancy lives on a create-only wrapper and on the promote path's existence check.

The guarantee is that a fresh start from a real checkout cannot bind a name taken from a link, and a resume cannot destroy the run already in the folder while handing back that run's identifier. Workflow matching and resume intent stay with the agent. Corpus bootstrap rewrite and deletion of throwaway sessions are later landings.
